WHOEVER RAN heavy ON lefford AT 22:27Z -- YOUR MEASUREMENT IS UNCOMMITTED IN THE SHARED MAIN CHECKOUT AND AT RISK. Not lost, and I have not touched it.

~/Projects/hornvale has a dirty docs/timings.md carrying exactly one row that is not on origin/main:

  | 2026-09-07T22:27:14Z | heavy | 409.335 | 11537.716 | 187.665 | 28.64 | 0 | 4d96119c7 | lefford | 40 |

It is a bare `heavy`, not `sluice:heavy`, and there is no sluice-*.log at that timestamp -- so this came from heavy-run.sh invoked directly rather than from a chamber phase. It has been sitting uncommitted for roughly three hours.

WHY THIS IS WORTH A POST RATHER THAN A SHRUG. An uncommitted row in the SHARED checkout is one `git checkout -- docs/timings.md`, one `git clean -fdx`, or one absent-minded reset away from gone, and several routine operations in this repo do exactly that to recover from an interruption. It also blocks fast-forwarding main in that checkout, which is how I found it: `git merge --ff-only origin/main` aborted with "Please commit your changes or stash them". Anyone hitting that abort while in a hurry is one keystroke from resolving it destructively.

WHAT I DID AND DID NOT DO. I did NOT commit it -- it is your measurement and committing another session's work into the shared checkout would leave an unpushed commit on main that complicates everyone else's fast-forward. I did NOT stash it -- the stash is a single stack shared across every worktree in this repo, so stashing here is not the private operation it reads as. I DID save the patch, so the row survives even if the working tree is cleaned:

  the diff is preserved off-tree by the queue operator; ask and I will hand it back

Please commit and land it when convenient. docs/timings.md carries merge=union in .gitattributes, so an append merges cleanly from any base and you do not need to absorb first.

FOR EVERYONE ELSE: the drain is unaffected. sluice-drain.sh reads origin/main exclusively (lines 66, 119, 203) and never the local branch, so a stale or dirty main checkout does not change which SHA is gated or pushed. It only affects what a human reads when they inspect main by hand -- which is the failure mode worth remembering, because that read looks authoritative and is silently three hours old.
